Hi Jane,

Thanks again for taking the call today — great to meet you and the Acme AI team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we stay aligned: 

What we covered
- Primary ask: comparative reliability / SLO behavior across Redwood vs hyperscaler-managed inference endpoints (uptime, rate limits, error budgets, failover).
- Your constraints: enterprise SLA, multi-region failover requirements, and a procurement timeline for Q2 procurement.

High-level differentiators (see attached PDF for head-to-head):
- Redwood Dedicated: SLA-backed 99.95% uptime for reserved capacity, predictable per-token pricing, and configurable autoscale/burst policies.
- Hyperscalers: often advertise higher SLA on multi-tenant endpoints (99.99%), but performance can vary under noisy neighbor conditions and cross-region failover is typically heavier (longer cold-starts).
- Failure modes: Redwood supports graceful degradation via model-variant fallback + prefix/KV cache preservation to reduce error surface. We also support cross-region failover for Private/Dedicated customers with <30s failover in our tests (depends on warm pool).

Proposed next tests (what we recommend you run):
1) Sustained throughput run: 10k tokens/sec sustained for 30 minutes against the dedicated pool to validate error budget usage.
2) Burst/limit test: simulate 1k concurrent short requests to validate throttling behavior and 429 patterns.
3) Failover: orchestrated regional outage to observe failover latency and state preservation (KV cache impact).

Attached: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-comparison.pdf, slo_matrix.xlsx, and a short reliability_test_plan.md.

Next steps
- Confirm the test window you prefer (we typically recommend early Tues/Wed US hours).
- Share any procurement contact (if different from procurement@acmeai.com) and any IP/network constraints for Private deployment tests.
- We'll spin up a dedicated test pool on our side and share temporary API keys + a Drive folder with the harness.

Happy to sync with Marissa (CS) and Rishi (SRE) on the details — I've cc'd them.

Best,

Jane — quick answers inline: 

1) Rate limits: For Dedicated (reserved capacity) we enforce limits at the customer-pool level by default (per-tenant). We can also provision API-key level throttles for shared pools. 429s include a Retry-After header with a recommended backoff; our SDKs auto-retry with exponential backoff by default (configurable).

2) Error budgets / Console: yes — the Redwood Console exposes an error-budget dashboard (per-route/model) that shows burn rate, historical 429/5xx counts, and rolling SLO windows. Data is exportable as CSV and we can push to your SIEM via our tracing hooks.

3) Failover & KV cache: cross-region failover uses async replication for KV caches to keep latency low; in practice this means a small window where hot-cache keys may miss after failover but model state (KV structure) is preserved and we rehydrate hot keys from prefix cache within ~5-20s depending on traffic. For Private installs we also support configurable synchronous replication (depending on network topology) if you need stronger guarantees — this has a higher cross-region latency cost.

SLOs we typically see in production (subject to commitment level):
- Hosted multi-tenant API: soft SLO ~99.9% (no SLA)
- Dedicated reserved pool: SLA-backed 99.95% uptime, with defined error budget and credits for sustained outages.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): SLA negotiated per contract, often 99.95%+ with joint runbook.

Suggested acceptance criteria for the tests:
- Sustained throughput: 0% 5xx, <0.1% 429 across 30m steady load at target throughput.
- Burst: bounded 429 rate with clear Retry-After behavior and SDK retries succeeding within 10s.
- Failover: recovery to steady-state QPS within 60s, and KV cache warm-up time measured.

Marissa and Rishi will coordinate the test harness + credentials. We'll provision a temporary dedicated pool and share keys.

—Ben
